entries.title: Landing-page hero copy
entries.description: Conversion-focused hero section with voice, audience, and structure constraints.
entries.idea: Write landing page hero copy for a meal-prep subscription for busy parents
entries.template:
You are a direct-response copywriter. Write hero-section copy for a weekly meal-prep subscription aimed at working parents of young kids.

Deliver exactly:
1. A headline under 10 words that leads with the outcome (evenings back, not "meal kits")
2. A subheadline under 25 words naming the audience and the mechanism
3. One CTA button label, 2-4 words, first person

Voice: warm, plain-spoken, zero corporate jargon, no exclamation marks. Do not mention price. Avoid the words "delicious", "easy", and "solution".

entries.title: 30-day social calendar
entries.description: A structured content calendar with pillars, formats, and hooks.
entries.idea: Create a 30-day Instagram content calendar for a small fitness studio
entries.template:
Act as a social media strategist for a neighborhood fitness studio (audience: locals 25-45, mixed fitness levels). Build a 30-day Instagram calendar.

Format: a table with columns Day | Content pillar | Format (reel/carousel/story) | Hook (first line, under 12 words) | CTA.

Rules: rotate 4 pillars — member stories, quick workouts, myth-busting, behind-the-scenes; no more than 2 promotional posts per week; every hook must create curiosity or name a specific pain; write hooks in second person.

entries.title: Python automation script
entries.description: A production-quality script request with error handling and style constraints.
entries.idea: A Python script that renames files in a folder based on their creation date
entries.template:
Write a Python 3.11 script that renames every file in a target folder to the pattern YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS_originalname.ext based on file creation time.

Requirements:
- argparse CLI: positional folder path, --dry-run flag that prints the rename plan without touching files
- Handle name collisions by appending _1, _2…
- Skip hidden files and subdirectories
- Use pathlib only (no os.path), type hints throughout, and a main() guard
- On any per-file error, log to stderr and continue; exit code 1 if any file failed
Output only the complete script in one code block, no explanation.

entries.title: Accessible React component
entries.description: Typed, tested component request with a11y and API constraints.
entries.idea: Build a React autocomplete input component with keyboard navigation
entries.template:
Build an accessible autocomplete text input in React 18 + TypeScript.

API: <Autocomplete options={string[]} value onChange onSelect placeholder />.
Behavior: filter options case-insensitively as the user types; highlight the active option; full keyboard support (ArrowUp/Down, Enter to select, Escape to close); close on outside click.
A11y: combobox/listbox ARIA pattern with aria-activedescendant, aria-expanded, and a visually hidden status region announcing result counts.
Styling: CSS modules, no UI libraries. Include a brief usage example. Keep the component under 200 lines.

entries.title: API endpoint documentation
entries.description: Consistent, example-rich REST documentation from a code snippet.
entries.idea: Document a REST API endpoint from its Express handler code
entries.template:
You are a technical writer. I will paste an Express route handler. Produce API reference documentation with exactly these sections:

## Endpoint — method + path
## Description — 2-3 sentences, plain language, lead with what it's for
## Request — parameters table (name, in, type, required, description) and a realistic JSON body example
## Responses — one subsection per status code with a realistic JSON example and when it occurs
## Errors — table of error codes with the exact condition that triggers each

Infer unstated behavior from the code only; where the code is ambiguous, flag it with **[verify]** rather than guessing.

entries.title: Difficult professional email
entries.description: Tone-calibrated email for a delicate situation.
entries.idea: Write an email declining a project extension request from an important client
entries.template:
Write an email to a long-term client declining their request to extend the project deadline by three weeks.

Context: we have a hard dependency on a vendor slot that cannot move; we CAN offer a reduced-scope on-time delivery plus a fast-follow release.
Tone: warm but unambiguous — the decline must be clear in the first two sentences, not buried.
Structure: acknowledge the request, decline with the one-sentence reason, present the alternative with concrete dates, end with a collaborative next step.
Length: under 160 words. No apologizing more than once, no corporate filler ("per my last email", "circling back").

entries.title: SEO blog post outline+draft
entries.description: Structured long-form post with search intent and voice constraints.
entries.idea: A 1,500-word blog post about beginner indoor plant care
entries.template:
Write a 1,500-word blog post: "Indoor Plants for Beginners: A No-Guilt Guide to Not Killing Them".

Audience: first-time plant owners in apartments. Search intent: informational, keyword "indoor plants for beginners" (use naturally ≤5 times).
Structure: hook that names the reader's fear of killing plants; H2 for each of 5 beginner plants (include light, water cadence, one failure mode each); H2 troubleshooting table (symptom → cause → fix); short buying checklist; closing that gives permission to lose a plant occasionally.
Voice: funny-but-useful, second person, contractions, no listicle clichés ("without further ado"), no em-dash overuse.

entries.title: Plain-English contract summary
entries.description: Faithful simplification with risk flags and structure.
entries.idea: Summarize a freelance contract in plain English with risk flags
entries.template:
You are a paralegal writing for a non-lawyer freelancer. I will paste a contract. Produce:

1. **One-paragraph gist** (under 80 words)
2. **Your obligations** — bullet list, each with the source clause number
3. **Their obligations** — same format
4. **Risk flags** — anything unusual or one-sided (auto-renewal, IP assignment breadth, indemnity, non-compete scope), each rated Low/Medium/High with a one-line why
5. **Questions to ask before signing** — max 5

Rules: never paraphrase a clause number you're unsure of — quote it; do not give legal advice, describe what the text says; if a standard clause is MISSING (payment terms, kill fee, late fees), flag that too.

entries.title: Socratic study tutor
entries.description: A patient tutor persona that teaches by questioning.
entries.idea: A patient tutor that helps a 9th grader understand algebra without giving away answers
entries.template:
You are a patient, encouraging algebra tutor for a 9th grader. Your goal is understanding, not answers.

Method: when I bring a problem, never solve it outright. First ask what I've tried. Then guide with one question at a time, each question small enough that I can answer it. If I'm stuck twice on the same step, give a worked example of a SIMILAR problem (different numbers), then return to mine.
Tone: warm, zero condescension; celebrate correct reasoning, not just correct answers.
Always end a session by asking me to explain the solved problem back to you in my own words, and correct any gaps in my explanation.

entries.title: 50-minute lesson plan
entries.description: Complete classroom plan with timings, checks, and differentiation.
entries.idea: A 50-minute middle school lesson plan about the water cycle
entries.template:
Create a 50-minute lesson plan on the water cycle for a 7th-grade science class of ~28 students.

Format with these exact sections: Learning objectives (3, measurable, "students will be able to…"), Materials, Timeline (minute-by-minute table: 0-5 hook, 5-20 direct instruction, 20-40 activity, 40-50 assessment + exit ticket), Group activity (hands-on, uses only common classroom materials), Differentiation (one support for struggling students, one extension for advanced), Exit ticket (3 questions: one recall, one application, one drawing).
Constraint: the hook must be a demonstration or question, never a video.

entries.title: Flashcards + quiz generator
entries.description: Spaced-repetition-ready cards and a leveled quiz from any material.
entries.idea: Turn my biology notes into flashcards and a practice quiz
entries.template:
I will paste study notes. Convert them into study materials:

Part 1 — Flashcards: 12-20 cards as a table (Front | Back). Fronts must be questions or cloze deletions, never headings; backs under 25 words; no card may test two facts at once.
Part 2 — Quiz: 8 questions in ascending difficulty — 3 recall MCQs (4 options, plausible distractors), 3 application questions, 2 short-answer synthesis questions. Answer key at the end with one-line explanations of WHY each wrong MCQ option is wrong.
If my notes contain an apparent error or contradiction, list it under "Check your notes" instead of putting it on a card.

entries.title: UX microcopy pass
entries.description: Rewrites interface copy with voice, length, and state constraints.
entries.idea: Rewrite error messages and empty states for my app to be helpful and human
entries.template:
You are a UX writer. I will paste interface strings (errors, empty states, confirmations). Rewrite each one.

Rules per string: lead with what happened or what to do — never "Oops" or "Something went wrong" alone; give the ONE next action; max 12 words for errors, 20 for empty states; no blame ("you entered an invalid…" → "that email doesn't look right"); no humor in destructive or payment flows.
Output a table: Original | Rewrite | What changed (3-6 words). Then flag any string whose real problem is the flow, not the copy.

entries.title: User interview guide
entries.description: Non-leading discovery interview script with probes.
entries.idea: A user interview script to learn why customers abandon onboarding
entries.template:
Create a 30-minute user-interview guide investigating why users abandon our product's onboarding.

Structure: intro script (consent, no-wrong-answers framing, recording ask); 5 warm-up minutes on their context; core section with 8-10 open questions strictly about PAST behavior ("walk me through the last time…"), each with two follow-up probes; a 5-minute wrap with the magic-wand question and anything-we-didn't-ask.
Hard rules: no leading questions, no hypotheticals ("would you use…"), no feature pitching, no question answerable with yes/no. After the guide, add a 5-point checklist for the interviewer on staying neutral.

entries.title: One-page PRD
entries.description: Tight product requirements doc with scope fences.
entries.idea: Turn my feature idea into a one-page PRD with scope and success metrics
entries.template:
You are a senior product manager. I'll describe a feature idea; turn it into a one-page PRD.

Sections: Problem (2-3 sentences, evidence-based framing), Who it's for (primary persona + trigger moment), Success metrics (1 primary, 2 guardrails, with target numbers as [placeholders]), Solution sketch (what it does, not how it's built — max 5 bullets), Explicitly OUT of scope (min 3 items — infer the tempting adjacencies and fence them off), Open questions (max 4), Launch risks (top 2 with mitigations).
Total under 450 words. Where I haven't given you information, write [assumption: …] rather than inventing facts silently.

entries.title: Data analysis persona
entries.description: A rigorous analyst persona with methodology constraints.
entries.idea: An analyst that reviews my metrics and finds insights without overclaiming
entries.template:
You are a skeptical senior data analyst. I will share metrics, tables, or dashboard screenshots.

For each analysis: separate OBSERVATIONS (what the data literally shows) from INTERPRETATIONS (what it might mean) under distinct headings; every interpretation gets a confidence level (high/medium/low) and the alternative explanation you'd want to rule out; name the single most useful follow-up query or data pull.
Never: extrapolate beyond the date range shown, treat correlation as causation, or average ratios without flagging the weighting problem. If sample sizes are small, say so before anything else.

entries.title: SQL query builder
entries.description: Readable, correct SQL with edge-case handling.
entries.idea: Write a SQL query for monthly retention cohorts from an events table
entries.template:
Write PostgreSQL for monthly retention cohorts.

Schema: events(user_id bigint, event_name text, occurred_at timestamptz). "Active" = any event in the month. Cohort = month of a user's first-ever event.
Output: cohort_month, months_since_signup (0-11), active_users, retention_pct (of cohort size, 1 decimal).
Requirements: CTEs with meaningful names over subqueries; date_trunc for months; handle users active in non-consecutive months correctly (classic retention, not consecutive); exclude cohorts younger than the months_since offset (no partial denominators); comment each CTE in one line. Then explain the trickiest part of the query in 3 sentences.

entries.title: Chart → narrative
entries.description: Turns a chart into an honest executive narrative.
entries.idea: Turn this chart into three bullet points for an executive update
entries.template:
I will share a chart (image or described data). Write the executive narrative.

Deliver: a headline finding (one sentence, includes the magnitude — "up 23%", not "up significantly"); three supporting bullets, each ≤20 words, ordered by business impact; one caveat bullet starting "Watch out:" naming the most important limitation (seasonality, sample, denominator change…).
Rules: numbers over adjectives; compare to a stated baseline, never to vibes; if the chart's axes are truncated or the data can't support a causal claim I've implied, say so explicitly instead of complying.

entries.title: Animated explainer scene
entries.description: A text-to-video scene with camera, motion, and style directions.
entries.idea: A short animated scene of a paper boat sailing down a rainy street gutter

Camera: low tracking shot at water level following the boat, slight handheld feel. Style: soft painterly 3D animation, warm streetlight reflections on wet asphalt, gentle rain streaks, cozy melancholy mood. Motion: steady 4-second track, then the boat spins slowly once in an eddy, then continues. No text, no people, no logos.

entries.title: Product demo storyboard
entries.description: A 60-second demo video script with shots and voiceover.
entries.idea: A 60-second product demo video script for a budgeting app
entries.template:
Write a 60-second product demo video script for a personal budgeting app.

Format: table with columns Time (5-10s blocks) | Shot (screen recording vs lifestyle b-roll, with framing) | On-screen text (≤6 words) | Voiceover (conversational, ≤25 words per block).
Arc: 0-10s the pain (checking account anxiety, no app yet); 10-45s three features MAX, each shown solving one specific moment; 45-60s social proof line + CTA.
Rules: voiceover reads like a friend, not a narrator ("you know that feeling when…"); never say "seamless", "powerful", or "all-in-one"; the CTA names the free tier.

entries.title: Cinematic trailer shot
entries.description: A single hero trailer shot with precise camera grammar.
entries.idea: An epic cinematic trailer shot of a lone rider crossing a desert at dusk
entries.template: Cinematic trailer shot, 6 seconds: a lone rider on horseback crests a massive dune at dusk, silhouetted against a deep orange sky, sand streaming off the ridge in the wind. Camera: slow aerial pull-back and rise, starting close on the rider and revealing the vast empty desert. Lighting: low sun, long shadows, atmospheric haze. Style: anamorphic widescreen, filmic color grade with teal shadows and amber highlights, subtle lens flare. Mood: solitary, mythic. No text overlays, no other characters.
